title: व्यतिरेक वितरणका आधारमा ब्याँसीभाषाका वर्ण निर्धारण byatirek bitaranka aadhaarmaa byaasibhaasaaka barna nirdhaaran
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख व्यासी ‘रं’ शौका भाषाको व्यतिरेक वितरणका आधारमा ब्यासी भाषाको वर्ण निर्धारणमा केन्द्रित छ । ब्याँसी भाषा चिनियाँ–तिब्बती भाषा परिवारको पश्चिमी हिमाली अन्तर्गत पर्ने शौका ‘रं’ समुदायको भाषा हो । ब्याँसी भाषामा ६ ओटा स्वर वर्ण र २९ वटा व्यञ्जन वर्ण रहेका पाइन्छन् । यी सबै वर्णहरूमा व्यतिरेक रहेको पाइन्छ । प्रस्तुत लेखमा ब्याँसी भाषाका छ वटा स्वर वर्णलाई जिब्राको उचाइ, जिब्राको सक्रियता र ओठको गोलाइका आधारमा व्यतिरेक गरी वर्ण निर्धारण गरिएको छ । २९ वट२९ वटा व्यञ्जन वर्णलाई उच्चरण स्थान, उच्चारण प्रयत्न, घोषत्व र प्राणत्वका आधारमा व्यतिरेक गरी वर्ण निर्धारण प्रक्रियाको विश्लेषण गरी निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । ब्याँसी भाषाका अ, आ, इ, उ, ए, ओ गरी ६ वटा स्वरवर्ण जिब्राको सक्रियता, जिब्राको उचाइ र ओठको अवस्थाका आधारमा व्यतिरेकी रहेका, यस्तो व्यतिरेक पदादि, पदमध्य ब्याँसी ‘रं’ शौका भाषाको संरक्षण गर्नुका साथै भाषा अध्येताहरूलाई आधार सामग्रीको रूपमा सहयोग पु¥याउने अपेक्षा राखिएको छ ।
american_english: The present article is focused on phoneme determination of the Byansi language on the basis of contrastive distribution in the Byansi 'Rang' Shauka language. The Byansi language is the language of the Shauka 'Rang' community, falling under the West Himalayish branch of the Sino-Tibetan language family. In the Byansi language, 6 vowel phonemes and 29 consonant phonemes are found to exist. A contrast is found to exist among all these phonemes. In the present article, phonemes are determined by contrasting the six vowel phonemes of the Byansi language on the basis of tongue height, tongue position, and lip rounding. The 29 consonant phonemes were contrasted on the basis of place of articulation, manner of articulation, voicing, and aspiration, and conclusions were drawn by analyzing the phoneme determination process. With the 6 vowel phonemes of the Byansi language—a, ā, i, u, e, o—being contrastive on the basis of tongue position, tongue height, and lip condition, and such contrast occurring word-initially and word-medially, it is expected to help preserve the Byansi 'Rang' Shauka language as well as provide reference material to support language scholars.

informal_english: This paper is all about sorting out the phonemes of the Byansi language by looking at contrastive distribution in the Byansi 'Rang' Shauka tongue. The Byansi language belongs to the Shauka 'Rang' community, which sits under the Western Himalayish branch of the Sino-Tibetan family. Turns out Byansi has got 6 vowel phonemes and 29 consonant phonemes. Every single one of these phonemes shows proper contrast. In this paper, the six vowel phonemes get sorted by contrasting them against tongue height, tongue activity, and lip rounding. The 29 consonants were contrasted based on place of articulation, manner of articulation, voicing, and aspiration, wrapping up by analysing how the phonemes get established. With the 6 vowels in Byansi—a, ā, i, u, e, and o—contrasting based on tongue activity, tongue height, and lip position, and popping up word-initially and mid-word, the hope is this will help keep the Byansi 'Rang' Shauka language safe as well as giving language researchers a solid bit of reference material to lean on.
